questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Inexact Differentials?
questions.answer: An inexact differential is a differential expression that does not come from a single potential function on the region being used. Its accumulated value can depend on the path, as heat and work often do in thermodynamics.

questions.prompt: What does \(\delta Q\) mean in Inexact Differentials?
questions.answer: In Inexact Differentials, \(\delta Q\) means small transfer of heat, written with delta to mark path dependence. Its unit is J.

questions.prompt: State a central formula or test for Inexact Differentials.
questions.answer:
The inexact condition is
\[M_y\ne N_x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad M\,dx+N\,dy\text{ is not exact}\]
